title: Visual Anything package file
description: The contents of a `.vapackage` file: components and relation types from one domain, shared as a unit.

version.description: Which version of the package this is, as a semantic version such as `1.2.0`. A package copied from another project keeps it, so that updating it from there can say what changed.

license.description: The license its components, relation types and images are shared under (ADR 0047). What ships with Visual Anything always says, with one of the licenses ADR 0047 allows; a project's own packages may leave it out.

attribution.description: Who made it and where it comes from, as its license asks them to be credited, such as "Icons by Jane Doe, CC-BY-4.0". The app shows it with the package, and exports carry it for the packages a view uses.

crosswalks.description: Tables that map one scheme of external identifiers to another, for importers (ADR 0056).

images.description: The images its components' appearances, and elements' own appearances, show. Each is data only: nothing in it runs or refers to anything outside it. Left out when there are none.

solids.description: The solids its appearances show (ADR 0075): each one's definition, its file kept beside the project as `solids/<hash>.glb`. Left out when there are none.

code.description: The package's code: one module of JavaScript, one item per line, which may export the hooks `attributes`, `check` and `draw`. The file only holds it: it runs only once the person approves it, by the SHA-256 of its text and its capabilities, in an interpreter inside WebAssembly, and never while the file is read. Left out when the package has none.

capabilities.description: What its code may reach beyond its element, each approved by the person on its own. Left out when it needs nothing more.

extensions.description: What its code adds to the app beyond its components (ADR 0089): actions, importers, exporters and panels, declared here so that the app lists them before the code is approved or runs. Each runs through a hook of the code: `act`, `importFile`, `exportFile` or `panel`. Left out when it adds none.

conflicts.description: What a merge could not join, as data (ADR 0072): each conflict says which item it is about, what the file keeps in place, and the other choice. Written only by a merge; the person resolves them.

Id.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

PackageVersion.description: A semantic version: three numbers, as in `1.2.0`, optionally followed by a pre-release after a hyphen, as in `2.0.0-beta.1`.

LicenseId.description: A license, by its SPDX identifier, such as `CC0-1.0`, `CC-BY-4.0`, `MIT` or `Apache-2.0`, or a `LicenseRef-` name of one's own.

derivesFrom.description: The component this one derives from: another component, or `essence`.

ids.description: What it is in other catalogs, by scheme (ADR 0056); absent when it has none.

attributes.description: The attributes this component adds to the ones it inherits.

simulation.description: What it can simulate (ADR 0085), worked out tick by tick by its package's code; inherited whole, and replaced whole by declaring another.

Component.description: The reusable definition of a kind of element. It inherits everything it does not redefine.

propertyNames.description: A scheme of external identifiers: a short lowercase name for someone else's catalog, such as `uberon` or `fma`.

ExternalIds.description: What an element, a component or a relation type is in other catalogs, by scheme, such as `{ "uberon": "UBERON:0002135", "fma": "FMA:7235" }`. Search finds by them, importers match by them, and nothing ever follows them.

ExternalId.description: An identifier in someone else's catalog, such as `UBERON:0002135`. It is data, never followed.

type.description: A `destination` holds a  {@link  Destination } : a value that opens something when followed.

default.description: The value an element or relation has when it does not set its own.

choices.description: For a string attribute, the values it is expected to take, offered in this order. Any other value only produces a warning.

unit.description: For a number attribute, the unit its values are in, written after them on shapes, such as "ms" or "GB".

format.description: For a string attribute, how its values are written (ADR 0082): `plain`, the default, as the characters they are; `emphasis`, with text emphasis (`**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~struck~~`, `` `code` ``, `==highlight==`, `++underline++`) wherever they are drawn. Identifiers, SQL and names stay plain.

AttributeDefinition.description: An attribute that a component or relation type defines.

shape.description: The kind of its shapes. While its shapes draw their contents as rows, any kind other than `rounded-rectangle` is drawn as a rectangle.

width.description: The width of its shapes when a view does not set one, in canvas units.

height.description: The height of its shapes when a view does not set one, in canvas units. Shapes that draw their contents as rows take their height from their rows instead.

detail.description: What its shapes write under the element's name. Each part is inherited on its own.

textPlacement.description: Where its shapes place the block of the element's name and detail inside their label area, with an inset of 8 units (ADR 0082): from its top, centred, or ending at its bottom. Essence sets `middle`. Containers and rows write their header at the top whatever it says.

contentsAsRows.description: Whether its shapes draw the elements they hold as rows: one under another below a header, as wide as the shape, in the model's order, as a table draws its columns. Rows have no positions of their own in views, and the shape's height follows its rows.

connectionPoints.description: Where relations attach to its shapes: each relation attaches to the one facing its other end. An empty list has relations attach anywhere on the border, whatever is inherited. Shapes that draw their contents as rows attach relations beside their header and their rows instead.

image.description: The image its shapes show; `none` shows none, whatever is inherited.

solid.description: The solid its shapes show (ADR 0075), drawn in place of an image when both are given; `none` shows none, whatever is inherited.

geometry.description: Its shapes' own outline, drawn in place of their kind (ADR 0066); `none` takes an inherited one away, so that the kind is drawn again.

part.description: The named part of an SVG image its shapes are drawn as (ADR 0067); `none` takes an inherited one away.

levels.description: What its shapes show as the canvas zooms (ADR 0055): levels by the scale each starts at, the highest reached winning, and below the first a silhouette. An empty list follows the canvas's own steps, whatever is inherited; left out, they are inherited.

expandFrom.description: The scale from which a collapsed container of this appearance expands while the canvas looks into it, collapsing again below 90% of it (ADR 0055). Neither is stored: the view keeps it collapsed.

face.description: What its shapes show inside their body, written in a subset of HTML and CSS and laid out by Visual Anything itself (ADR 0083); `none` takes an inherited face away. Each of its parts is inherited on its own.

borderWidth.description: The width of its shapes' border, in canvas units, over the drawing defaults' (ADR 0088); 0 draws no border.

dash.description: How its shapes' border is drawn (ADR 0088), as a relation's line is.

cornerRadius.description: The corner radius of its shapes, in canvas units, over the drawing defaults' (ADR 0088). It rounds rectangles of either kind; ellipses, cylinders, people and free geometry ignore it.

opacity.description: How opaque its shapes are, from 0.2 to 1 (ADR 0088). Their text stays whole.

shadow.description: Whether its shapes cast a soft shadow, over the drawing defaults' (ADR 0088).

gradient.description: A fill that runs from the fill to a second color (ADR 0088); `none` takes an inherited one away.

text.description: How its shapes write the element's name (ADR 0088). Each part is inherited on its own.

Appearance.description: How an element's shapes are drawn. Whatever an appearance leaves out is inherited.

Color.description: A color written as `#RRGGBB`: no alpha, no short form and no names. Files may write the digits in either case; the program writes new colors in capitals and keeps a color's spelling when it is set to the same color again.

componentName.description: Whether it writes the component's name. Essence writes it.

attributes.description: The attributes whose values it writes, in this order, after the component's name; an attribute without a value is skipped.

badges.description: The badges it writes after the values, each while its element meets the badge's condition.

lines.description: The most lines the detail takes, from 1 to 6; Essence gives 3. Its last line ends with "…" when the text is longer.

DetailRules.description: What a shape writes under its element's name, wrapped to at most `lines` lines; the whole of it shows on hover (ADR 0082).

Badge.description: A short text, such as "PK", that a shape writes while its element meets the badge's condition.

attribute.description: The name of a boolean attribute of the element.

AttributeBadge.description: A badge written while a boolean attribute of the element is true.

RelationEndBadge.description: A badge written while the element is the `from` end of a relation of this relation type, or of one derived from it.

name.description: Unique among the connection points of one appearance, such as "in" or "out".

at.description: Where it sits along its side, from 0 at the side's left or top end to 1 at its right or bottom end.

ConnectionPoint.description: A named place on the border of a shape where relations attach.

image.description: The id of an image that a package in use defines.

placement.description: `icon`, the default: small, beside the name, inside the shape. `drawing`: on a plate in place of the shape, with the name under it. `parts`: the picture under the shape's header, its contents anchored to its named parts drawn in their places (ADR 0067). Shapes that draw rows always show it as an icon in their header, and rows as a small icon before their name.

tint.description: When set, the picture is drawn as a silhouette of this colour: its shape kept, its colours replaced.

placement.description: `icon` beside the name, `drawing`, the default, on a plate above a name band, or `parts`, under the header of a drawing with parts.

camera.description: In place of the solid's own camera.

lighting.description: `studio`, the default, or `flat`: base colors without light.

azimuth.description: Degrees around +Y, 0 looking from +Z, glTF's front, toward −Z.

elevation.description: Degrees above the horizon, or below it when negative.

zoom.description: 1 fits the solid's bounds with a margin of 4%; left out, 1.

target.description: The point it turns around; left out, the middle of the bounds.

projection.description: `perspective`, with a vertical field of view of 30°, when left out; or `orthographic`.

SolidCamera.description: How a solid is looked at: from a direction, fitted to its bounds (ADR 0075).

SpacePoint.description: A point in a solid's space, in meters, +Y up, rounded to a tenth of a millimetre.

width.description: The width of the box its coordinates are written in, like an SVG view box from its top left.

keepProportions.description: Whether its box keeps its proportions, centred in the shape; otherwise it is stretched to it.

label.description: Where its shapes write the name and the detail, in the box's coordinates.

FreeGeometry.description: A shape's own outline (ADR 0066): closed contours written in a box of their own, drawn filled and stroked in the shape's colors, a contour inside an odd number of others cut out as a hole.

d.description: SVG path data, with M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A and Z, absolute or relative.

PathContour.description: Contours as SVG path data: each subpath one contour, closed whether or not it ends with Z.

points.description: Three points or more, as x,y pairs.

PolygonContour.description: A polygon, its points written as SVG writes them.

GeometryLabel.description: A rectangle of free geometry's box.

part.description: The part's id in the image, or its name in the solid.

image.description: The image that names it; left out with `solid`, the image or solid the element's container shows with its parts.

solid.description: The solid that names it, in place of `image` (ADR 0075).

PartReference.description: A named part of an SVG image or of a solid, as an appearance draws its shapes as one (ADR 0067, ADR 0075). It names the image or the solid, never both.

from.description: The scale it starts at, where 1 is 100%: it is entered there, and left only 10% below it.

shows.description: What shows from it: a silhouette only, or any of the name, the detail (its attributes and badges, written under the name), the contents or rows, the image, and the face (ADR 0083), which a shape with a face draws in place of its name and detail.

face.description: The variant of the face it shows, by its id; absent, the face's own markup (ADR 0083).

LevelOfDetail.description: What shapes show from a scale up.

LevelPart.description: One thing a shape shows at a level of detail.

FaceVariantId.description: The id of a face's variant.

size.description: `content`: the face's height is the shape's height, as rows give a table its height. `shape`, the default: it is laid out in the shape's size and cut where it overflows.

markup.description: Its markup, a line each, so that git shows the lines a change touched. Its caps are the core's, which a command refuses past and opening only warns about: 200 lines and 16 KiB, its variants' included.

style.description: Its style rules, a line each, shared by its variants: at most 128 rules and 16 KiB.

variants.description: Other markups, at most 8, each with an id, which levels of detail and collapsed containers show.

collapsed.description: The id of the variant a collapsed container shows on its sheet.

Face.description: A component's face (ADR 0083): markup in strict XHTML, filled from the element's name and attributes through `{{…}}` slots, and style in a subset of CSS. Nothing in it runs and nothing in it is fetched. Each part left out is inherited.

FaceLine.description: One line of a face's markup or style, without its line ending.

FaceVariant.description: Another markup of a face, sharing the face's style.

Gradient.description: A fill that runs from the shape's fill to `to`, down or to the right (ADR 0088).

font.description: The typeface: the drawing defaults' two, or Roboto Mono.

size.description: The name's size, in canvas units.

align.description: How its lines are aligned across the label area.

position.description: Where the name is written: inside the shape, or in a tag beside it, attached above, below, to its left or to its right. A name that does not fit inside still moves to a tag below.

color.description: The name's color; a color under 4.5:1 on its fill is pointed out, never refused.

border.description: The line around the name's back.

wrap.description: Whether the name wraps onto more lines; otherwise it is cut with "…".

padding.description: The space between the label area's edge and the text, in canvas units.

TextStyle.description: How a shape writes its element's name (ADR 0088). Whatever it leaves out comes from the component, then the drawing defaults. Emphasis inside text stays Markdown (ADR 0082); these apply to the whole name.

tick.description: How long one tick stands for; left out, one tick of no unit.

ticks.description: How many ticks a run plays unless the person asks for more: 100 when left out.

SimulationDefinition.description: What a component can simulate: its parameters, its simulated values with their limits, how long a tick stands for and how many ticks a run plays. A component inherits it whole from the one it derives from, and replaces it whole by declaring its own.

default.description: The value a run starts from unless another is chosen: of its type, within its range.

min.description: For a number, the lowest it may be.

max.description: For a number, the highest it may be.

step.description: For a number, the step its control moves by.

unit.description: For a number, the unit it is in, such as "items/s".

choices.description: For a choice, the values it may take, offered in this order.

ParameterDefinition.description: A value a simulation run starts from, which the person, a view state or Claude chooses.

ParameterValue.description: A parameter's value: a number, a boolean, or one of its choices.

ParameterChoice.description: One of a choice parameter's choices.

name.description: Its name; one named like an attribute of the element is read in its place while a run is shown.

min.description: For a number, its lowest limit: a tick that answers less stops the run.

max.description: For a number, its highest limit: a tick that answers more stops the run.

unit.description: For a number, the unit it is in.

choices.description: For a string, the values it may take: a tick that answers another stops the run.

SimulatedValueDefinition.description: A value each tick answers, such as a queue's length.

TickLength.description: How long one tick stands for, such as 1 s or 1 day.

derivesFrom.description: The relation type this one derives from: another relation type, or `relates-to`.

ids.description: What it is in other catalogs, by scheme (ADR 0056); absent when it has none.

nests.description: Whether its relations place their `from` element inside their `to` element, as "is part of" does.

attributes.description: The attributes this relation type adds to the ones it inherits.

limits.description: What its relations may connect. Breaking a limit only produces a warning.

RelationType.description: The reusable definition of a kind of relation. It inherits everything it does not redefine.

width.description: The line width, in canvas units.

route.description: The style of its relations' automatic routes (ADR 0069), over the view's; `orthogonal` undoes an inherited one.

opacity.description: How opaque its lines are, from 0.2 to 1 (ADR 0088). Their labels stay whole.

RouteStyle.description: How a line runs between its ends: square corners, straight, or a smooth curve.

RelationTypeLimits.description: What the ends of a relation type's relations may be. A list left out is inherited from the relation type this one derives from, and sets no limit when none sets one; `any` sets no limit on that end, whatever is inherited. Breaking a limit only produces a warning.

LimitList.description: The ids of the components or relation types an end may be created from. An end created from one of them, or from anything derived from one of them, keeps within the limit.

from.description: The scheme its keys are in.

to.description: The scheme its values are in; never the same as `from`.

source.description: Where the table comes from, in words, such as the release of the crosswalk it was made from.

entries.description: Each identifier of `from` with the identifier of `to` it maps to.

Crosswalk.description: A table that maps the identifiers of one scheme to another's, such as `uberon` to `fma`, used by importers to fill in the schemes a file lacks.

IdScheme.description: A scheme of external identifiers: a short lowercase name for someone else's catalog, such as `uberon` or `fma`.

propertyNames.description: An identifier in someone else's catalog, such as `UBERON:0002135`. It is data, never followed.

CrosswalkEntries.description: A crosswalk's identifiers of one scheme, each with the one of the other scheme it maps to.

ImageDefinition.description: A picture a package defines, kept as the core cleaned it.

id.description: Starts with its package's id, as in `clinic.whatsapp-logo-k3f9q2`.

source.description: Where it comes from, such as "Simple Icons" or "Drawn for Visual Anything".

license.description: The license it is shared under, by its SPDX identifier (ADR 0047). Every image of a built-in package says, with one of the licenses ADR 0047 allows.

width.description: The width of its view box, which with its height gives its proportions.

height.description: The height of its view box.

svg.description: Its SVG text as the core cleans it: one `svg` element with a `viewBox`, elements and attributes from an allow-list only, and references only to its own parts.

SvgImage.description: A picture drawn from SVG: shapes, paths, gradients, clipping and masks only.

id.description: Starts with its package's id, as in `clinic.front-desk-4fj2ka`.

license.description: The license it is shared under, by its SPDX identifier (ADR 0047).

width.description: Its width in pixels, as its header gives it.

height.description: Its height in pixels, as its header gives it.

BitmapImage.description: A picture kept as the bytes of a PNG, JPEG or WebP file, without its metadata.

id.description: Starts with its package's id, as in `robotics.arm-k3f9q2`.

description.description: Its text alternative, which the outline, the inspector and announcements give with its shapes.

source.description: Where it comes from, such as "Drawn for Visual Anything".

license.description: The license it is shared under, by its SPDX identifier (ADR 0047).

hash.description: The SHA-256 of its cleaned file, in lowercase hexadecimal, which names the file `solids/<hash>.glb`.

bytes.description: The size of its file, in bytes.

parts.description: Its named parts, in depth-first order.

camera.description: The camera its pictures are drawn from, unless an appearance gives its own.

animations.description: Its animations, in its file's order; left out when there are none.

SolidDefinition.description: A solid a package defines, kept as the local program cleaned it (ADR 0075).

SpaceBounds.description: The smallest box, along the axes, that holds every vertex of a solid or a part.

SolidCounts.description: What a solid's file holds, counted as the core reads it.

name.description: The node's name, as cleaning keeps or makes it.

parent.description: The index, in the solid's `parts`, of the part that holds it; left out for a part held by none.

point.description: The vertex of its own geometry nearest the middle of its bounds: where relations end and its name is written. Left out for a part that draws nothing of its own.

SolidPart.description: A named part of a solid: one of its named nodes, holding the node's own geometry and everything below it that is not a named part of its own (ADR 0075). Its name is its id.

SolidAnimation.description: One animation of a solid: keyframes that move its nodes.

CodeLine.description: One line of a package's code, without its line ending.

Capability.description: Something a package's code may reach beyond its element: `model:read`, the whole model, read-only; `time`, the clock; or `network:` and one web origin, such as `network:https://status.example.com`, fetched through the local program.

actions.description: Its actions, which answer changes the person reviews before they apply.

importers.description: Its importers, which read a file into changes the person reviews.

exporters.description: Its exporters, which write the model and a view as a text file.

panels.description: Its panels, which the inspector shows for a selection.

PackageExtensions.description: What a package's code adds to the app (ADR 0089), each list left out when empty.

where.description: Where it is offered: the canvas menu for a selection, the Packages menu, or both.

components.description: The components whose elements, or those of components derived from them, it is offered for in the canvas menu; left out, it is offered for any selection.

PackageActionDeclaration.description: A named action, run with the selection and, with `model:read`, the model (ADR 0089).

ExtensionId.description: The id of something a package adds, unique among the package's ones of its kind.

ExtensionLabel.description: What the app names something a package adds, in the package's own words.

extensions.description: The extensions it reads, each with its dot, in lower case, such as ".sql".

PackageImporterDeclaration.description: An importer: it reads files with these extensions into changes (ADR 0089).

FileExtension.description: A file's extension, with its dot, in lower case.

PackageExporterDeclaration.description: An exporter: it writes the model and a view as a text file with this extension (ADR 0089).

components.description: The components whose elements, or those of components derived from them, it shows for; left out, it shows for any one selected element.

PackagePanelDeclaration.description: A panel the inspector shows for a selection of these components' elements (ADR 0089).

item.description: The item, by a key local to its file: `world`, `element:<id>`, `relation:<id>` or `order` in the model file; `package`, `component:<id>`, `relation-type:<id>` or `image:<id>` in a package file; `view`, `position:<element>`, `position:<element> in <container>`, `free-shape:<id>`, `stacking:<container>` or `route:<relation>` in a view file; `scenario`, `step:<id>`, `tour`, `tour-step:<id>`, `thread` or `comment:<id>` in theirs; `project` in the project file.

path.description: Where the value lies inside the item, as a list of keys; empty for the whole item.

kept.description: Whose value the file holds in place.

other.description: The other side's value; left out when that side removed the item.

base.description: The common ancestor's value; left out when it had none.

sides.description: The names git gave the two sides, when it gave them.

FileConflict.description: What a merge of one project file could not join (ADR 0072). The file in place is a valid file of its kind; `other` and `base` are JSON as that kind of file holds the item, checked only when chosen.

ConflictReason.description: Why a merge could not join: both sides changed a value differently; one removed what the other changed; both added an id with different values; a removal meets what needs what it removes; two additions close a containment cycle; or both sides reordered a list differently.

ConflictSides.description: The names of a merge's two sides, as git gave them.
